title: The Tale of the Bloody Benders
summary: Josh and Chuck (with Jerry) cover the Bloody Benders, a family of suspected serial killers who ran a remote tavern and inn along the Osage Trail near Cherry Vale, Kansas, in the 1870s. The episode was suggested by listener Star White. It covers the family's background and aliases, the early body discoveries in Drum Creek, the disappearance of Dr. William York and George Newton Longcore's daughter Mary Anne, the search that uncovered the cellar and orchard graves, the alleged method of killing travelers at a curtained table, the vigilante theories and the twelve arrested men, the family's unknown fate, and later preservation efforts and cultural references. The episode ends with a listener mail segment from Tanya Vanderpool about a dental visit.

segments.title: Opening and listener suggestion
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the Halloween-themed episode, joking about the 'murder family' name, and credit listener Star White from Kansas for suggesting the Bloody Benders after seeing signs in Montgomery County. They mention the book Hell's Half Acre.

segments.title: Settling the Bender family and tavern
segments.summary: The hosts describe post-Trail of Tears Kansas as a frontier where outcasts settled. John Bender Sr., his son John Bender Jr. (who used aliases), and the women Elvira ('Ma') and Kate arrived and built a small tavern and inn on a claim along the Osage Trail near what became Cherry Vale. The family was known as odd, and sold goods and produce from their orchard.

segments.title: Violent Kansas and the first bodies
segments.summary: The hosts explain that 1870s Kansas was violent and travelers often vanished unnoticed. In May 1871 a man's body with a smashed skull and cut throat was found in Drum Creek, followed by more bodies, including William Jones, who had about $250 meant for his mortgage. The Bender family was regarded as strange but not suspected.

segments.title: The woman who escaped barefoot
segments.summary: In February 1873 a woman stopped at the Bender home, was offered a table of pistols and knives as her 'supper', and ran barefoot for about two miles to get help after claiming she needed to step outside. The family's reaction did not raise alarm at the time.

segments.title: Disappearance of Dr. William York and the search
segments.summary: George Newton Longcore and his eighteen-month-old daughter Mary Anne vanished on the way to Iowa. Their neighbor, physician William York, investigated and then disappeared too. His brother-in-law-type connection to Colonel Alexander York, a Civil War colonel and Kansas senator, led to a search of about seventy-five men. John Bender Jr. led them to a tree with bullet marks, and Ma Bender reportedly accused the earlier woman of being a witch.

segments.title: Discovery of the cellar and graves
segments.summary: The family had fled by train before the search reached their house. Searchers found a trap door, a stone cellar with blood and a rotting smell, and then bodies in the orchard and well, including William York and Longcore and Mary Anne. Authorities eventually linked the family to as many as twenty-one murders. The hosts describe the curtained seating method, with travelers silhouetted by candlelight and struck from behind, and bullet holes found in the house.

segments.title: Aftermath, vigilante theories, and fate of the Benders
segments.summary: The case became a national media sensation and a dark tourism draw. Twelve men were arrested for alleged receiving of stolen goods, and a vigilante group called the Regulators was suspected, with bodies posed with hands on chest. Modern research suggests Ma was Almira Meek and Kate was Eliza Griffith. The family's fate remains unknown, with many rumors. Laura Ingalls Wilder's family story is noted as unlikely. The site was later bought by Bob Miller, who wants archaeological surveys.

segments.title: Pop culture and sources
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the 2022 movie Bender, a Red Dead Redemption pig farm inspired by the Benders, a Neil Gaiman American Gods reference, and the genealogy site recommended for period newspaper accounts.

segments.title: Listener mail from Tanya Vanderpool
segments.summary: Tanya Vanderpool writes that she started listening after a friend recommended the show and that her dentist became a fan after she mentioned the Chow Chilla bus kidnapping episode. The hosts joke about her 'Land of Ten Thousand Lakes' sign-off.
